_note: The DSX Scene BIND corpus (dsx-scene.md P5): data-driven children as data. THE ROW LAW: <group bind="expr" key="field"> instantiates its template children once per array row; a non-array binds zero rows; a dict row keys on String(row[keyField] ?? index), a scalar row on String(row); duplicate keys get the ·1/·2… suffix in encounter order (the <list> keying law verbatim); rows past 256 (SCENE_BIND_LIMIT) drop with one diagnostic. THE KEYED-IDENTITY LAW: a key present on both sides of a reconcile keeps its instantiated subtree across any reorder (diff cases pin added/removed/retained as data). THE SCOPE LAW: inside a row, item.* resolves against the row value exactly like a <list> row (scope cases pin per-row resolved props through the ordinary hole resolver); a row node's on:* handlers run in the row scope, so the payload carries the row item (surface-tested — a data corpus cannot mount handlers). Removing a row removes its subtree and STOPS ITS ANIMATIONS (surface-tested). Nested binds are full rows of rows. Runners: TS (per-PR). Kotlin/Swift are the NAMED P5 follow-up.
